text: The book's glossary calls a specific element of the domain for which predicate P fails, thereby disproving a universal statement ∀x P(x), a ___.
explanation: Per the book, a counterexample is a specific domain element for which P fails, which disproves ∀x P(x). It is the dual of a witness — a specific element for which P holds, which proves ∃x P(x). Supplying a witness would establish an existential, not refute a universal.
